checks.finding: The recovery verifier rejects invalid UTF-8, non-canonical JSONL, unknown record shapes, mixed ledger identities, invalid event or checkpoint digests, sequence discontinuity, and predecessor discontinuity before hydration.
The derived event, epoch, checkpoint, idempotency, and head indexes are rebuilt deterministically from verified records and remain disposable projections rather than source authority.
A non-empty stream is recoverable only when its final record is a valid checkpoint; malformed, blank, torn, tampered, and uncheckpointed tails block visibly.
Recovery rechecks the exact source digest after opening the append sink and before hydrating the ledger, closing the verified-read to append-open race within the declared single-process boundary.
Recovered events, epochs, and checkpoints retain exact identities, historical epochs replay byte-deterministically, and the next append continues the recovered sequence and predecessor chain.
Negative cases preserve the original log bytes; recovery exposes no repair or truncation operation and never silently discards an invalid tail.
The file-backed Codex wrapper and CLI recover the configured ledger before wrapper turn handling, reject an invalid startup tail, and record only compact recovery metadata in diagnostic state.
Recovery and index rebuilding are local structural operations with zero model, provider, network, evaluator, effect, or authority-owner calls.
Recovery records, indexes, replay results, assessments, and Codex startup metadata declare authority_effect none and grant no effect or owner authority.
Parent-owned independent replay matched all 29 selected paths, byte counts, and SHA-256 digests; artifact identifiers and paths are unique.

The selected Product Capability records, business meanings and relations, DomainSpec nodes, lifecycle orchestration, recovery boundary, generated system nodes, bridge edges, and recovery realization close under deterministic two-run projection.
All nine ARE package suites, the Codex regression, and the continuous-construction integration remain green with no skipped tests after recovery integration.
On this host with Node v26.8.1, the existing complete warm Codex context-lifecycle benchmark measured p95 94.263 ms against the 250 ms target; this is local evidence, not a universal guarantee.

residue: Recovery is strict and fail-closed; corrupt, incomplete, or uncheckpointed logs require an explicit separately designed repair path.
Cross-process locking, multi-writer coordination, compaction, branching, reduction, and distributed durability remain unimplemented.
Recovery provides process continuity and reuse of exact reasoning state; it does not create a durable CyberAlchemy Session.
The repository profile remains memory-backed unless file storage or a reasoning-state log path is explicitly configured.
The app-server gateway and wrapper remain candidate integrations; supported installation and deployment are separate work.
claim_limit: Independent bounded conformance evidence for ARE-REASONING-STATE-RECOVERY-IMPLEMENTATION-BINDING-001 only. It does not accept the binding, adopt the Product Capability, admit an ontology, prove whole-engine closure, install or activate a default, publish, deploy, create Session authority, or authorize runtime or external effects.
